newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-DEL PIERO GOAL GIVES JUVENTUS WORLD CLUB CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEL PIERO GOAL GIVES JUVENTUS WORLD CLUB CUP.

text.p: Juventus won the World Club Cup final for the second time in their history on Tuesday when an 82nd-minute goal from Alessandro Del Piero gave them a 1-0 win over River Plate of Argentina.
The Italians, playing with seven of the men who won the European Cup final in May, had the better of a scrappy match but one which they undoubtedly deserved to win.
The only goal came eight minutes from time when Angelo Di Livio's corner was flicked on to Del Piero lurking unmarked on the far side of the box.

The 22-year-old striker turned and controlled the ball and in the same movement sent it soaring past River Plate goalkeeper Roberto Bonano who had no chance of stopping it flying past his left-hand shoulder into the far corner of the the net.
The goal belatedly brought the match to life and Alen Boksic had two good chances to score after trademark Juve counter-attacks but wasted them both.
River Plate went close at the other end in the later stages but the nearest they came to a goal was when Ariel Ortego hit the crossbar from an acute angle after 72 minutes.

Juventus followed Ajax's success for Europe in this final last year. Since the competition began in 1960, South American sides have won it 20 times against Europe's 14. Juventus's previous victory came in 1985 when they beat Argentinos Juniors on penalties.

River Plate: 1-Roberto Bonano; 4-Hernan Diaz, 6-Eduardo Berizzo, 2-Celso Ayala, 3-Juan Sorin, 5-Leonardo Astrada, 8-Roberto Montserrat, 11-Sergio Berti (18-Leonel Gancedo 75), 10-Ariel Ortega, 9-Enzo Francescoli, 7-Julio Cruz (Marcelo Salas 84)
